flagged.title: The Atlantic Economy: Trade, Tobacco and Piracy
flagged.reason: The video explicitly claims both on screen and in narration that the Piracy Act 1717 established colonial vice-admiralty courts and ended the requirement to ship pirates to London, directly contradicting the corrected facts and misattributing the powers granted under the 1698 Act.

mark_affecting.quote: 1717: Piracy Act establishes colonial courts. [...] Before the 1717 Piracy Act, if you caught a pirate you had to ship them all the way back across the Atlantic to London for a trial. [...] These new courts allowed pirates to be tried quickly, right there on-site in the colonies.

mark_affecting.quote: Fast forward to the 1760s, there were over 40 of them.

flagged.title: After Victory: Frontier and Tax Tensions, 1763–64
flagged.reason: The video states that General Amherst directly ordered the distribution of smallpox blankets (contradicting the corrected lesson text where the garrison acted independently) and falsely attributes the quotation 'taxation without representation is tyranny' to James Otis's 1764 pamphlet.

mark_affecting.quote: General Amherst himself ordered the distribution of smallpox-infected blankets to Indigenous warriors.
a lawyer named James Otis published a pamphlet objecting to the Act, and it gave us this totally iconic quote: 'Taxation without representation is tyranny.'
